title: indigo_mount_synscan: a coordinates request admitted during park, home or auto home is overwritten with OK before it is refused
description:
Found on 2026-11-21 by the reviewer of ticket 3beb3554-f847-4155-b5e7-5bed700096f0 (closed, commit 296992891); present on master before that ticket. A MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES request admitted while a park, home or auto home runs claims nothing in on_change_request (only a sync, or a slew starting from idle, is claimed). The home finalizer (time-critical, due 0.2 s after the home handler) or the next poll can run before the queued GoTo handler (normal priority): it ends the motion, sets global_mode to IDLE and publishes OK over the request's BUSY; the handler then refuses with 'Mount is moving' after the motion has ended. The client sees BUSY, OK, ALERT. Observed as an intermittent failure of synscan_mount_goto_admitted_during_homing_is_refused in recorded runs (114/113, 117/116) until the test released its gate from the request's BUSY publication, which removed the accidental exposure but not the defect.

To do: reproduce deterministically in the simulator suite (hold the request's handler behind the finalizer), then either refuse the request before BUSY in on_change_request or claim every admitted request until its handler runs; all coordinates states through indigo_update_coordinates(), client targets never rewritten. Bump the driver version; recorded simulator run.

outcome.summary: Fix verified. reject_change on MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES (.driver:2070-2073) generates INDIGO_REJECT_COORDINATES_CHANGE_IF(global_mode == SYNSCAN_GLOBAL_HOMING, 'Mount is homing') after the parked guard and before on_change_request and the copy macro (.c:2759). While the coordinates are not BUSY, a request during a home is refused through indigo_reject_coordinates_change() before anything is admitted; during an auto home, which publishes the coordinates BUSY itself, it gets only the message. There is no library or generator change (reject_change is an existing DSL feature used by other drivers). Version 29->30 (0x1E), and the .c delta matches the .driver delta. MIGRATION_STATUS is 119->121 with the Comment column untouched; the README and TEST_SUMMARY record matches. Tests: in a scratch copy (own Makefile.inc, scratch dylibs), the ticket's test source built against the master driver (v29) fails goto_during_homing and sync_during_homing ('first publication after the request is not the refusal'), while goto_during_parking passes (characterization: the parked guard already refuses it). Against the ticket driver all three pass, as does tracking_request_survives_home_finalizer with the generalized gate hook. The cases hold the queue with an urgent gate queued from the busy light and wait on property revisions; the 0.3 s wait that lets the finalizer come due is intentional and bounded. Races (non-blocking, all pre-existing, none made worse): global_mode is read on the bus thread (reject check, then the on_change_request claim) and written by check-then-set on the queue (home, park and auto-home handlers, and the finalizers) without a common lock. (1) Home admitted but its handler not yet run: a request reads IDLE, claims SLEWING and is admitted; the home handler then refuses itself (global_mode != IDLE) and the GoTo runs. The result is consistent, no B,O,A. (2) If the home handler sets HOMING between the reject read and the on_change_request read, the request is admitt

history.text: Writing reverse-order reproducer: finalizer before GoTo/sync handler during home/park
Running new during_homing/during_parking cases against unfixed driver v27
Running new cases on v27 (before) and v28 (after) binaries
Running full synscan simulator suite (unrecorded) on v30 tree
Comparing refused_goto_keeps_alert on v27 and v30 (5 runs each)

Implementer (claude-opus-5-5): Reproduction: new cases in indigo_test/integration/test_mount_synscan_simulator.c hold the device queue with an urgent gate right after the home/park handler, send the coordinates request, keep the gate 0.3 s so the 0.2 s finalizer comes due, then release (finalizer, TIME priority, runs ahead of the request's NORMAL handler). Against driver v27 (HEAD 9202eb54c driver built as a separate binary with the same test source): synscan_mount_goto_during_homing_is_refused FAILS with coordinates BUSY, OK, ALERT ('Mount is moving'); synscan_mount_sync_during_homing_is_refused FAILS (sync admitted: BUSY, BUSY, then ALERT); synscan_mount_goto_during_parking_is_refused PASSES on v27 - the park request copies MOUNT_PARK.PARKED=true at admission, so the generated parked-mount guard already refuses any coordinates request before BUSY during a park; the defect is homing only (MOUNT_HOME and MOUNT_AUTOHOME, both global_mode HOMING). Fix: reject_change { condition = PRIVATE_DATA->global_mode == SYNSCAN_GLOBAL_HOMING; message = 'Mount is homing'; } on MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES -> INDIGO_REJECT_COORDINATES_CHANGE_IF: refusal through indigo_reject_coordinates_change() before the copy and BUSY when the coordinates are not BUSY, BUSY message only when the homing already published BUSY (auto home). GoTo and sync are both refused during homing (a sync would bind the request to a moving position; once the poll publishes the homing's BUSY the framework guard drops them anyway). Version 30 per coordinator (landing after e2f19dd5). After fix: the 3 cases pass; full suite unrecorded run 118/119 - one intermittent failure of synscan_mount_refused_goto_keeps_alert (GoTo after a refused GoTo did not reach OK), unrelated code path (no homing), passed 5/5 on v27 and 5/5 on v30 in targeted reruns. Pre-existing residual race noted, not fixed: the on_change_request slew claim (read IDLE, write SLEWING in bus context) and the home/park/autohome handlers' check-then-set of
Merging master (e2f19dd5, c3aeb19f) into ticket branch
Recorded run: tools/run_driver_test.py mount_synscan on merged tree (v30)

Merged master 545ce57f6 (e2f19dd5 v29, c3aeb19f b7083ad38) into the ticket branch (merge commit f98e1bdfc, no rebase): only conflicts were version (resolved 30) and the generated .c (master's taken, regenerated with the worktree generator). MIGRATION_STATUS 119 -> 121 on top of master. Interaction with b7083ad38: the HOMING reject_change is emitted before INDIGO_COPY_TARGETS_PROCESS_COORDINATES_CHANGE and returns, so a request during a homing whose BUSY is published gets one BUSY message ('Mount is homing') only, never the copy macro's 'Mount is busy' as well (code inspection, not a dedicated test). Recorded run on the merged tree: 2026-11-21 17:56 3.0.0.30 mac arm64 simulator 121/121 OK; synscan_mount_refused_goto_keeps_alert passed (the earlier single intermittent failure did not recur, cause not found).

reviews.notes: Fix verified. reject_change on MOUNT_EQUATORIAL_COORDINATES (.driver:2070-2073) generates INDIGO_REJECT_COORDINATES_CHANGE_IF(global_mode == SYNSCAN_GLOBAL_HOMING, 'Mount is homing') after the parked guard and before on_change_request and the copy macro (.c:2759). While the coordinates are not BUSY, a request during a home is refused through indigo_reject_coordinates_change() before anything is admitted; during an auto home, which publishes the coordinates BUSY itself, it gets only the message. There is no library or generator change (reject_change is an existing DSL feature used by other drivers). Version 29->30 (0x1E), and the .c delta matches the .driver delta. MIGRATION_STATUS is 119->121 with the Comment column untouched; the README and TEST_SUMMARY record matches. Tests: in a scratch copy (own Makefile.inc, scratch dylibs), the ticket's test source built against the master driver (v29) fails goto_during_homing and sync_during_homing ('first publication after the request is not the refusal'), while goto_during_parking passes (characterization: the parked guard already refuses it). Against the ticket driver all three pass, as does tracking_request_survives_home_finalizer with the generalized gate hook. The cases hold the queue with an urgent gate queued from the busy light and wait on property revisions; the 0.3 s wait that lets the finalizer come due is intentional and bounded. Races (non-blocking, all pre-existing, none made worse): global_mode is read on the bus thread (reject check, then the on_change_request claim) and written by check-then-set on the queue (home, park and auto-home handlers, and the finalizers) without a common lock. (1) Home admitted but its handler not yet run: a request reads IDLE, claims SLEWING and is admitted; the home handler then refuses itself (global_mode != IDLE) and the GoTo runs. The result is consistent, no B,O,A. (2) If the home handler sets HOMING between the reject read and the on_change_request read, the request is admitted unclaimed, and the original B,O,A is still possible, but only in a window of a few instructions; before this fix the window was the whole homing. (3) The implementer's leftover is real and pre-existing (identical claim on master). The claim reads IDLE and writes SLEWING after the home handler's check but before its write of HOMING, so the handler goes on to set HOMING over it; or the claim writes SLEWING after HOMING, in which case the home finalizer returns on global_mode != HOMING without rescheduling, so MOUNT_HOME stays BUSY. Both need a sub-microsecond interleaving. This change does not affect that window; if wanted, fix it separately by making global_mode transitions atomic (claim under the device lock or with a compare-and-swap). The opposite case, HOMING still set for up to 0.2 s after the axes stopped, refuses a request only while MOUNT_HOME is still BUSY, so that refusal is legitimate. Refusing a sync during homing loses nothing legitimate: before the fix it was admitted and added an alignment point at a moving position. Kept ALERT: a refusal sets the keep flag without a preceding BUSY of the request. In a real homing the next poll publishes the homing's BUSY, which clears it, and the homing ends OK, as the documented rule (cleared by a new request or a motion seen by the poll) intends. In the test's zero-length homing no BUSY intervenes, so the finalizer's OK is published as the kept ALERT; that is also per the rule. NON-BLOCKING: the helper's final assertion (state != BUSY) accepts either outcome, so asserting the expected state would pin it; and there is no auto-home case for the message-only branch (checked by code inspection). No client targets are rewritten and no other frame's values are published. Formatting follows AGENTS.md.
